newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Pioneer fund's '96 net falls to PLN 85 mln.
newsitem.headline: Polish Pioneer fund's '96 net falls to PLN 85 mln.

text.p: The Pioneer First Polish Trust Fund Company, owned by Boston-based Pioneer Group, saw the net profit of its balanced fund fall to 85.4 million zlotys in 1996 from 121.9 million zlotys in 1995, the fund said on Wednesday.
Pioneer, which launched operations in 1992 as Poland's first open-ended fund, said in a statement that its balanced fund's 1996 revenues fell to 111.2 million zlotys from 147.6 million two years ago.

It said that at the end of 1996 its balanced fund invested 31.6 percent of its portfolio in shares and rights, 31.7 percent in the government bond, 35.9 percent in treasury bills, 0.4 percent in mass privatisation certificates and 0.4 percent in other instruments.
The value of the balanced fund's participation unit increased by 51 percent to 75.23 zlotys during 1996.
Pioneer's aggressive fund netted 6.1 million zlotys since its launch in December 1995 on revenues of 11.1 million zlotys.

At the end of 1996, the aggressive fund's portfolio included 66.8 percent of shares and rights, 25.2 percent of treasury bills, one percent of mass privatisation certificates and seven percent of other instruments.
The value of the aggressive fund's unit increased by 79 percent to 18.21 zlotys from December 1995 until the end of 1996. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
